newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UK puts "interesting" defence idea to S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: UK puts "interesting" defence idea to S.Africa.

text.p: Britain has made "interesting" proposals on the sale of submarines and corvettes to South Africa, Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils said on Friday.

"The British have come up with an interesting package, it's not confined to Upholders (submarines) and to corvettes," Kasrils told a news conference at a maritime defence exhibition at Simonstown naval base.

"It's the kind of package which as a government we're interested in, not just as the ministry of defence. It's a kind of long-term, 25-, 30-year strategic package which is of interest to trade and industry, which is of interest to the development of our industry and economy," Kasrils said.
South Africa invited bids two years ago for four corvettes but negotiations were frozen when parliament decided to make a financial review of the country's defence needs.
Kasrils said initial phases of the review were nearly complete and Defence Minister Joe Modise expected to make a presentation on the military budget to parliament by the end of May.
Modise told the same news conference that his policy in arms buying was to form partnerships with foreign companies that would lead to investment and job creation in South Africa.
"We will be influenced by those companies who are going to go into partnership with us and who are going to help us overcome problems, particularly job creation," Modise said.

The chief of the navy, Vice-Admiral Robert Simpson-Anderson, said some of South Africa's surface craft and four Daphne-class submarines were so dated that the country had to scrounge for spares from the discards of other countries.

"We are scratching around on the scrap heaps of Europe to try to recover spares from Daphne submarines that the French are scrapping, we are searching the scrap heaps of Britain to see if we can recover spares from minesweepers," he said.
South Africa's naval weapons technology level was lower than that of at least two other sub-Saharan African countries, the admiral said.
Kasrils said that if government approval was granted for the purchase of new strike craft, the tendering process would be reopened.

Spain's Bazan was identified as the favourite in the first round of tenders, with Britain's Yarrow also a strong contender. Both are exhibiting in Simonstown, along with the German Frigate Consortium and GCN International of France.

Modise said Mozambique and Tanzania had asked South Africa for help in policing their waters to keep out foreign fish poachers, but the navy did not have the capacity to patrol even its own coast properly.
